rounds.text: Mayur Leather Products Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, as demonstrated by a compelling intrinsic value discount where a discounted cash flow model places value at Rs 95 per share against a market price of Rs 41.8, offering a 56.1% margin of safety [E39, E40]. The reverse DCF model highlights this mispricing, revealing that today's price implies a modest 7.0% earnings growth compared to the 18.0% assumed in the base case, leaving ample room for upward reassessment [E41]. Recent fundamental acceleration is striking, with compounded profit growth reaching 30% over 3 years and a dramatic 780% over the trailing twelve months [E16, E17], alongside strong profitability metrics including a 20.3% return on equity and an 8.03% return on assets that outpace sector benchmarks [E8, E9, E13]. Furthermore, capital expenditure has matured entirely with Capital Work in Progress dropping to zero, signaling that new capacity is now coming online to support future earnings [E35], all backed by a strong consumer durables sector tailwind score of +0.98 [E55, E56]. Conceded: debt exceeds net worth with a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.23x and promoter holdings have declined to 26.50% [E32, E36].

The valuation of Mayur Leather Products Ltd is stretched across multiple metrics, trading at an elevated P/E of 45.9x [E1] and a price-to-book ratio of 6.56x against a book value of ₹ 6.37 [E2], which is explicitly flagged as a negative by filed statements [E45]. This premium pricing rests on a foundation of dismal long-term profitability, demonstrated by a 10-year median return on equity of -27% [E22] and a 3-year median ROE of 0% [E24]. Financial structure also presents severe risks, as debt-to-equity stands at 1.23x where borrowings exceed net worth [E32], alongside warnings that the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E49]. Furthermore, operational quality is compromised by negative operating cash flow of ₹ -0.57 Cr in March 2026 [E29] and a cash conversion ratio of -0.50x [E28]. Most alarmingly, promoter confidence has cratered, with holdings dropping precipitously from 64.02% in September 2023 to just 26.50% by June 2026 [E36]. Conceded: [E39], [E40], [E41].

While the bear points to high headline valuation metrics [E1, E2], it overlooks that the P/E drops to an attractive 18.29x when viewed against the key ratios data provider [E6], while profitability metrics such as ROA at 8.03% and ROE at 14.16% comfortably outpace their respective sector benchmarks [E8, E9]. Conceded: [E22], [E24]. Addressing the financial structure concerns, borrowings actually decreased year-over-year to ₹ 3.88 Cr in March 2026 [E34], and the complete reduction of Capital Work-in-Progress to zero indicates that capex is fully finished, meaning new capacity is now coming online to drive future output [E35]. Furthermore, the bear's emphasis on operating cash flow ignores that free cash flow was positive at ₹ 0.84 Cr and operating cash flow reached 158% of operating profit in March 2026 [E30, E31]. Finally, the current market price of ₹ 41.8 leaves a substantial margin of safety of 56.1% relative to intrinsic DCF value [E39, E40], with a reverse DCF showing that current prices only demand a modest 7.0% earnings growth compared to the 18.0% base case assumption [E41].

Conceded: [E6]. The bull's focus on ROA and ROE benchmarks ignores the core structural reality that ROCE sits at an anemic 4.45% against a sector benchmark of 10.06% [E10], and long-term wealth creation is undermined by a 10-year median ROE of -27% and a 3-year median ROE of 0% [E22, E24]. While the bull highlights lower nominal borrowings, it glosses over the fundamental leverage risk that debt of ₹ 3.88 Cr exceeds net worth with a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.23x, alongside explicit warnings that the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E32, E34, E49]. The assertion that operating cash flow health is sound ignores the severe warning of negative operating cash flow of ₹ -0.57 Cr resulting in a negative cash conversion of -0.50x in March 2026 [E28, E29]. Furthermore, management's commitment to the business is deeply compromised by a massive promoter sell-off where holdings collapsed from 64.02% in September 2023 down to just 26.50% by June 2026 [E36]. Finally, relying on a model-driven margin of safety ignores that the stock is flagged for trading at an aggressive 6.56 times book value while facing decelerating earnings growth [E45, E54].
